This happens because the dependencies in the `tardis` environment are becoming old and the `conda` package manager is not-so-smart and can't handle them. 

The package can be installed using `mamba` or [using conda with the `libamamba` solver](https://www.anaconda.com/blog/a-faster-conda-for-a-growing-community) without problems. 

If you don't want to do that you could just checkout your TARDIS repository to the desired release and run `pip install .`

### What is the idea?

Currently `conda compare` works out of the box with `.txt`, `yml` or `.yaml` files, but not with `.lock` files made with `conda-lock`. A workaround is just change the file extension manually before doing the comparison.

### Why is this needed?

Because `conda-lock` provides `.lock` files, not `.txt`.

### What should happen?

`conda compare --name <env_name> conda-linux-64.lock`

Should return the comparison between the environment and the dependencies listed in the lockfile.

**Type:** :beetle: `bugfix` | :roller_coaster: `infrastructure`

I noticed the release date is incorrect when the day number ends with 0, for example `release-2023.02.2` corresponds to February 20th, 2023.

This was my mistake while trying to remove the `.0` of every new release, as Jaladh suggested. 

This was requested because to have a `.1` in the release name we should make two releases on the same day, and that does not happen frequently. Then, to simplify the names of most of our releases we stripped the trailing zero.

I don't know why `.rstrip()` works in that way. I used a simpler approach now that seems to work fine.
